title: MAP Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected an electrical fault or out-of-range signal from the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor fuel economy; Check Engine Light (CEL) on
actions: Inspect wiring and connectors to MAP sensor; Test MAP sensor output voltage; Replace MAP sensor
location: Near the throttle body

title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is lower than the normal operating range, suggesting a vacuum leak or sensor issue.
symptoms: Lean condition; Engine stalls at idle; Poor throttle response
actions: Check for vacuum leaks in intake manifold; Inspect MAP sensor wiring for open circuits; Test or replace MAP sensor
location: Near the throttle body

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is higher than the normal operating range, possibly indicating a sensor malfunction or wiring issue.
symptoms: Rich condition; Rough idle; Reduced engine power
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for shorts to voltage; Test MAP sensor output voltage; Replace MAP sensor if faulty
location: Near the throttle body

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a lower than expected voltage from the IAT sensor, indicating the intake air is colder than plausible or a circuit fault.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Difficulty starting in cold weather; Engine runs rich
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring for shorts to ground; Test IAT sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: Integrated into the airbox or intake manifold

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a higher than expected voltage from the IAT sensor, indicating the intake air is hotter than plausible or an open circuit.
symptoms: Reduced engine power; Hesitation during acceleration; Engine runs lean
actions: Inspect IAT sensor wiring for open circuits; Test IAT sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: Integrated into the airbox or intake manifold

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a voltage from the ECT sensor lower than expected, suggesting the engine is colder than plausible or a short in the circuit.
symptoms: Hard starting when cold; Rich fuel mixture; Reduced fuel efficiency
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring for shorts to ground; Test ECT sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a voltage from the ECT sensor higher than expected, suggesting the engine is hotter than plausible or an open circuit.
symptoms: Engine overheating (false reading); Lean fuel mixture; Cooling fan always on
actions: Inspect ECT sensor wiring for open circuits; Test ECT sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects an unusually low voltage signal from the Throttle Position Sensor (TPS), indicating the throttle is less open than plausible or a circuit fault.
symptoms: Poor throttle response; Engine hesitation; Stalling at idle

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects an unusually high voltage signal from the TPS, indicating the throttle is more open than plausible or an open circuit.
symptoms: Uncontrolled high RPM; Poor idle; Engine hesitation
actions: Inspect TPS wiring for open circuits or shorts to voltage; Test TPS output voltage across range; Replace TPS sensor
location: Attached to the throttle body

symptoms: Reduced fuel efficiency; Check Engine Light (CEL); Engine hesitation

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the heating element of the O2 sensor, which prevents it from reaching operating temperature quickly.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Delayed O2 sensor operation; Reduced fuel efficiency until warmed up
actions: Check fuse for O2 sensor heater; Inspect O2 sensor heater wiring; Replace O2 sensor

title: Fuel Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or electrical fault in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, meaning it's not firing.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough running; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring for open circuits; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector
location: Mounted in the throttle body or intake manifold

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary circuit controlling the fuel pump, preventing it from operating correctly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls while riding; No fuel pump prime sound
actions: Check fuel pump fuse; Inspect fuel pump relay and wiring; Test for power at fuel pump connector
location: Fuel pump relay typically under the seat or in the fuse box; wiring runs to the fuel tank

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal or an irregular signal from the crankshaft position sensor, which is vital for engine timing.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Intermittent stalling; No spark
actions: Inspect CKP sensor wiring for damage; Check CKP sensor for debris or damage; Replace CKP sensor
location: Near the crankshaft

title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal or an irregular signal from the camshaft position sensor, affecting valve timing and ignition.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Reduced engine power; Poor acceleration
actions: Inspect CMP sensor wiring; Check CMP sensor for debris; Replace CMP sensor
location: On the cylinder head

title: Ignition Coil "A" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder A (or single cylinder).
symptoms: Engine misfire; Loss of power; Rough idle
actions: Inspect ignition coil wiring; Test ignition coil resistance; Replace ignition coil or spark plug
location: Mounted on the spark plug (coil-on-plug) or frame (external coil with HT lead)

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal from the Vehicle Speed Sensor, leading to incorrect speed readings.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Incorrect gear indication; Cruise control not working (if equipped)
actions: Inspect VSS wiring and connections; Check VSS for physical damage; Replace VSS
location: On the gearbox output shaft or rear wheel (for ABS/Traction Control models)

title: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects that the Idle Air Control (IAC) system is not maintaining the desired engine idle speed.
symptoms: Unstable idle; Stalling at idle; High or low idle RPM
actions: Clean IAC valve and throttle body; Inspect IAC valve wiring; Replace IAC valve
location: Integrated into the throttle body assembly

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage (battery voltage) is consistently below the normal operating threshold.
symptoms: Dim lights; Difficulty starting; Electrical components malfunctioning
actions: Check battery voltage and charge; Test rectifier/regulator; Inspect alternator/stator output
location: Battery typically under the seat; Regulator/Rectifier mounted on the frame

title: System Voltage High
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently above the normal operating threshold, which can damage electrical components.
symptoms: Blown bulbs; Battery overcharging; ECU damage risk
actions: Test regulator/rectifier output; Check battery for overcharging; Inspect wiring for shorts to voltage
location: Regulator/Rectifier mounted on the frame

title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an issue with its internal serial communication or communication with other modules (e.g., ABS).
symptoms: Multiple warning lights; Intermittent system failures; Engine not starting
actions: Check all module connectors; Inspect CAN bus wiring for damage; Perform ECU diagnostic checks
location: Main wiring harness connecting ECU to other components

title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
problem: The ECU has detected an internal fault within its Read Only Memory (ROM), indicating a critical internal hardware or software issue.
symptoms: Engine not starting; Erratic engine behavior; Complete loss of engine control
actions: Attempt ECU software reflash; Check for power/ground issues to ECU; ECU replacement is often required
location: Main Engine Control Unit
column9: typically under the seat or fairing

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the circuit controlling the Check Engine Light (MIL) on the dashboard.
symptoms: Check Engine Light not illuminating; Check Engine Light always on; Inability to clear codes
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED on dashboard; Inspect wiring to dashboard; Diagnose ECU for output fault
location: Wiring from ECU to instrument cluster

title: Internal ECU Voltage Supply Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an internal issue with its own voltage supply, indicating a potential power regulation fault within the unit.
symptoms: Engine not starting; Intermittent engine cut-out; Multiple sensor errors
actions: Check main power and ground to ECU; Verify battery voltage stability; ECU replacement is often necessary
location: Main Engine Control Unit
column9: typically under the seat or fairing

title: Startup Failure
problem: The ECU detects that the engine failed to start within a specified number of attempts or time, even if all sensors read correctly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but doesn't fire; Repeated starting attempts fail; Difficulty starting in specific conditions
actions: Check fuel pressure; Inspect spark plugs and ignition system; Verify engine compression
location: General engine system

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Intermittent/Erratic
problem: The ECU detects inconsistent or erratic signals from the Vehicle Speed Sensor, leading to unreliable speed readings.
symptoms: Jumpy speedometer reading; Sudden speed fluctuations; Incorrect gear display
actions: Inspect VSS wiring for loose connections; Check for debris on sensor head; Replace VSS if signal remains erratic
location: On the gearbox output shaft or rear wheel

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit/Open
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or electrical fault in the motor controlling the electronic throttle plate.
symptoms: No throttle response; Engine enters limp mode; Engine stalls immediately
actions: Inspect throttle body wiring; Test throttle actuator motor resistance; Replace throttle body assembly
location: Integrated into the electronic throttle body assembly

title: Throttle Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a lower than expected voltage signal from a specific throttle position sensor (often a redundant sensor in fly-by-wire).
symptoms: Reduced engine power (limp mode); Inconsistent throttle response; Check Engine Light (CEL)

title: Throttle Position Sensor "D" Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a higher than expected voltage signal from a specific throttle position sensor (often a redundant sensor in fly-by-wire).
symptoms: Unintended acceleration (potential); Reduced engine power (limp mode); Check Engine Light (CEL)
actions: Inspect wiring for TPS sensor "D" for shorts to voltage; Test TPS "D" output voltage; Replace throttle body or sensor assembly
location: Integrated into the throttle body assembly

title: Throttle Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a lower than expected voltage signal from a secondary throttle position sensor (for redundancy in fly-by-wire).
symptoms: Limp home mode; Engine power reduction; Erratic throttle behavior
actions: Inspect wiring for TPS sensor "E"; Test TPS "E" output; Replace throttle body or sensor assembly
location: Integrated into the throttle body assembly

title: Throttle Position Sensor "E" Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a higher than expected voltage signal from a secondary throttle position sensor (for redundancy in fly-by-wire).
symptoms: Unintended acceleration risk; Reduced engine power; Check Engine Light (CEL)
actions: Inspect wiring for TPS sensor "E" for shorts; Test TPS "E" output; Replace throttle body or sensor assembly
location: Integrated into the throttle body assembly

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: This code specifically points to an electrical problem in the heater control circuit of the O2 sensor, preventing it from reaching operating temperature quickly.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Reduced fuel economy; Check Engine Light (CEL)
actions: Check O2 sensor heater fuse; Inspect wiring for continuity and shorts; Replace O2 sensor
location: Internal to the O2 sensor

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is consistently running with too little fuel for the amount of air, indicating a lean condition.
symptoms: Hesitation; Misfires; Reduced power and fuel economy
actions: Check for vacuum leaks (intake manifold
location: hoses); Inspect fuel pressure and fuel filter; Clean or replace fuel injector

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is consistently running with too much fuel for the amount of air, indicating a rich condition.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel smell; Reduced fuel economy
actions: Check for leaky fuel injector; Inspect fuel pressure regulator; Test O2 sensor for accurate readings
location: Fuel rail

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the circuit controlling the Evaporative Emission System (EVAP) purge valve.
symptoms: Check Engine Light (CEL); Fuel tank pressure issues; Poor idle (if valve stuck open)
actions: Inspect EVAP purge valve wiring; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace EVAP purge valve
location: Connected to the fuel tank vapor lines
column9: usually near the throttle body or airbox

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU determines that the catalytic converter is not operating efficiently enough to reduce emissions.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Check Engine Light (CEL); Reduced engine performance (less common for this code)
actions: Check for exhaust leaks; Verify O2 sensor readings; Replace catalytic converter
location: Integrated into the exhaust pipe

title: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
problem: The ECU's internal monitoring processor has detected a performance issue, indicating a critical internal hardware or software fault.
symptoms: Intermittent engine failures; Engine not starting; Erratic electrical behavior

location: Main Engine Control Unit
column9: typically under the seat or fairing

title: Generator Control Circuit Malfunction

location: Stator inside the engine cover; Rectifier/Regulator on the frame

title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit/Open

column9: typically sensing the shift drum position

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low
problem: The ECU detects a lower than expected voltage in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, indicating a short to ground or wiring issue.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Reduced engine power
actions: Inspect injector wiring for shorts to ground; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector
location: Mounted in the throttle body or intake manifold

actions: Inspect injector wiring for open circuits or shorts to voltage; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

actions: Inspect brake switch wiring; Test brake switch continuity; Replace brake switch

location: Starter relay typically under the seat or near the battery

title: Engine Failed to Start
